records.headline: The same answer, bit for bit, on the computers we tested
records.summary: Two AI models gave the same output on Linux, Windows and Mac computers.
records.method: Llama-2-7B, 16 prompts × 32 tokens: the same output on Linux, Windows and Intel Mac, with both the scalar and the AVX2 kernel (6 of 6 runs). On a shorter test (2 prompts × 4 tokens), Apple Silicon matched too: 8 of 8 runs across the four platforms. SmolLM3-3B: the same output on Apple Silicon Mac, Intel Mac, Linux and Windows, with the scalar and the SIMD kernel (8 of 8 runs), and an independent Python reference agreed. The same output means the same tokens and the same digest of every internal score at every step. GitHub-hosted CPUs; GPUs not covered.

records.headline: 169 payments a second, in our test lab
records.summary: Up from 3.4 a second on the same setup, with a fee change that is not on the live network yet.
records.method: 800 funded senders each kept one transfer in flight, measured over 60 seconds after a 15-second warm-up. With the once-per-block fee settlement from PR #133, the six validators completed 168.6 transfers a second; under today's rule they completed 3.4. Per the PR, only the before/after ratio is meaningful: absolute numbers depend on the hardware.
records.hardware: one 4-vCPU ubuntu-24.04 GitHub runner hosting all six validators
